story_log.title: Rays even ALCS 1-1 with 3-1 win over Guardians — Freddy Peralta 6 IP, Jose Ramirez costly error
story_log.development: CONTINUING [Day 10, TIER 1 ELIMINATION-ROUND GAME]: Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 3-1 per ground truth. Freddy Peralta: 6.0 IP, 4 H, 0 ER, 2 BB, 6 SO per StatMuse — has won his last 8 starts per StatMuse. José Ramírez two-out error in 5th let Rays score first run per TalkinBaseball/JomboyMedia — all three runs unearned. Liam Hicks 2-RBI single in 5th put Rays up 3-0 per TalkinBaseball/ClutchPoints. Chase DeLauter RBI single in 7th got Cleveland on board per ClutchPoints. Series tied 1-1, Game 3 Wednesday in Cleveland.

lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 10]: Reader knows this is the ALCS and saw Cleveland win Game 1 7-3. Today's new development: Rays even the series 3-1 behind Freddy Peralta's 6 scoreless and a two-out José Ramírez error that opened the door for all three unearned runs. Skip the series setup — lead with Peralta's streak (won last 8 starts per StatMuse) and the error that cost Cleveland. Cross-reference: how rare is it for a player of Ramírez's caliber (perennial MVP candidate) to commit a two-out, game-deciding error in a playoff game? Name other stars who've had similar playoff nightmares (Buckner 1986, A-Rod slap play 2004, etc.). The unearned-run angle is the story's irony: Guardians' elite pitching held Rays to 3, but their own defense gave them all away. Liam Hicks 2-RBI single was the dagger after the error. Chase DeLauter got Cleveland on the board in 7th but it was too late. Series now tied 1-1, heads to Cleveland for Game 3 Wednesday. What's at stake: this is a best-of-7, so winning at home is critical — Guardians need to protect home field in Games 3/4. Peralta was acquired from Mets at deadline per recent history — Milwaukee connection (he started Game 2 for Brewers in NLCS per recent history, now pitching for Rays). Ramírez had other rough moments in this series per recent history (struck out 19 times in Game 4 of ALDS per Oct 9 history, though that was a different game). The human element: Ramírez is beloved in Cleveland, this error will haunt him if Rays advance. The Tkachuk brothers combined for 9 points tonight per SportsCenter — tie that in as 'Meanwhile, in hockey...' if space allows, but it's a sidebar.

supporting_stories.headline: Flyers hit 0-8 after Kraken OT loss — worst start in 59-year franchise history
supporting_stories.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 2]: Reader knows Flyers were 0-7 entering tonight. New today: they lost to Seattle 2-1 in OT, falling to 0-8 — their worst start in franchise history (since 1967-68) per ground truth. This is also their 8th straight loss this season, last time they had 8+ within a season was 2023-24. The historical weight: how does 0-8 rank among worst starts in NHL history? (LA Kings are also 0-5 right now, their worst start ever.) Seattle is the inverse: 5-2 after 7 games, their best start in franchise history (since 2021-22). The Kraken won in OT. What's the path forward for Philly? They've now gone 8 games without a single point to open the season. Cross-reference: last time a team started 0-8 or worse and still made the playoffs? The desperation angle: when does the front office panic? Coaching change? Frozen Frenzy context: this loss happened during the NHL's big showcase night (all 32 teams in action), so the embarrassment is amplified.
